findings.reason: the broadened extraction belongs in the existing owner (extend its `<!-- landing-beat-examples -->` scope and table parse), not a parallel test file with a second copy of the extract-apply harness.
findings.text: §2's `tests/test_skills_cite_ops_the_store_accepts.py` re-implements machinery this owner already holds: op objects extracted from the skills and applied verbatim to a plan synthesised under a temp dir, with each op checked against `_OP_VOCAB` (`_required_fields` reads `_OP_VOCAB[op]` at line 1782; `_documented_examples` and `_apply_example`/`test_each_skills_documented_examples_apply` at lines 1825-1918), and the op-reference table already parsed at line 1814; `tests/test_mcp_vocabulary_is_complete.py:21` separately holds `_OP_VOCAB` against `_OP_DISPATCH`

findings.reason: the plan must extend or factor the existing reload owner (and name why an HTTP re-exec cannot carry a stdio session) rather than fork a second reload path.
findings.text: §3 (plan §3, write path `reckon/mcp_reload.py`) is a second owner of code-reload beside `reckon/serve.py`'s `_CodeReload`: `request_reload`/`finish` (lines 1508-1523) already detects a moved checkout (`_refuse_stale_code`, `_served_code_report`) and replaces the running image by re-exec on a stamp change; the plan does not cite it, and the snapshot owner `reckon/served_code.py` (`take_snapshot`/`served_report`/`drift`, used by serve.py) is likewise uncited

findings.reason: a body writer must state how a stored plan review's fingerprint still covers the section, or reuse a mechanism that already does, or the removal it re-adds recurs.
findings.text: §4's `set sections.<id>.body` (plan §4) adds a second section-body writer beside `_collapse_authored_section` (the one mechanism that rewrites a section's rendered extent), and the codebase deliberately removed the `collapse_section` op that "once rewrote the body" precisely to keep one fingerprint form (`tests/test_the_fingerprint_has_one_form.py:189` refuses it; owner of the guarantee is `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:678` `_fingerprint_forms`) — the plan's done-when checks `audit-doc` and untouched sibling bytes but says nothing about the review fingerprint

findings.reason: §7 already flags that the conflict payload may hold at base and requires reproduction before repair, so the design is unchanged; only the citation path needs correcting.
findings.text: §7 (plan §7) states "`_conflict_response` in `reckon/_mcp_tools.py` returns `current_version`", but `_conflict_response` is defined in `reckon/mcp_deadlines.py:862`; `reckon/_mcp_tools.py:248` is a `VersionConflictResult` Pydantic field, not the function

findings.reason: the honest change is to drop the alias or justify it, shrinking the added set-path surface rather than widening it twice.
findings.text: §4's `status` field on `set sections.<id>.<field>` "moves the declaration, as `set section_declarations.<id>` does" (same `_move_section_record` machinery at `reckon/_store.py:2502`), making it a second spelling of an existing accepted path with no statement of why the existing path cannot serve a status change

findings.reason: the sections must account for the added op surface in their own text, especially as the vocabulary was recently narrowed (`collapse_section` removed), not widened.
findings.text: §§5 and 6 each add a new op verb to the tool's discoverable vocabulary — `{op:'unset', path}` (§5) and `{op:'close', status, outcome, by[, superseded_by]}` (§6) — which enter `_OP_DISPATCH` (`reckon/_store.py:3172`) and `_OP_VOCAB` (`reckon/mcp.py:1367`, injected to clients at `mcp.py:635`), and neither section names a surface it retires or merges; §6 does not count, in its own text, the resolved-placeholder recipe as a retirement in the interface sense; the current week reads public_definitions 1824, cli_options 371, mcp_views 34, refusal_families 23

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `reckon/_store_section_ops.py` hides the section-title, body, followup, dependency, gate-measure, unset and close handlers behind the one op vocabulary, an interface smaller than the behaviour it carries.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2's new test, §3's new module and §4's section-body writer each re-implement shared machinery whose owner already exists.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1824, cli_options 371, mcp_views 34, refusal_families 23; §§5 and 6 add the `unset` and `close` op verbs to the discoverable op vocabulary without naming what they retire or merge.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched the store/mcp/skill area (§4 cites `insert_section`; §7 cites `_conflict_response`) but proposes `reckon/mcp_reload.py` without citing the reload machinery in `reckon/serve.py` or the snapshot owner `reckon/served_code.py`, and §7's `_conflict_response` citation names the wrong file.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4's `set sections.<id>.status` is a second spelling of the existing `set section_declarations.<id>` over the same declaration-move machinery, with no reason the existing path cannot serve.
